objectives: Recognise the wr spelling at the start of taught words.
Identify /r/ as the first spoken sound in wrap, wrist, and write.
Distinguish wr words from words beginning with /w/ or /r/ alone.
Use the whole word to confirm sound and spelling.
concepts: In these taught initial wr words, w is silent.
The spelling keeps w before r even though w is not pronounced.
The vowel and ending distinguish wrap, wrist, and write.

definitions.definition: A written letter that is not pronounced.
A letter or group of letters representing a sound.
A speech sound that can distinguish one word from another.

workedExamples.solution: The word begins with /r/; the w is silent.
Wrap keeps silent w in spelling.
The first spoken sound is /r/, not /w/.

commonMistakes: Pronouncing w in initial wr words.
Deleting w from the spelling because it is silent.
Guessing without listening to the first sound.
keyTakeaways: Initial w is silent in the taught wr words.
Check the rest of the word.
revisionPoints: w is silent in initial wr.
